details:
MARS EXPLORER – Detailed Project Description

1. Project Overview

MARS EXPLORER is an interactive web-based planetary exploration platform developed to support terrain understanding and route planning for future human missions to Mars. The application focuses on the Gale Crater region and uses NASA's Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter (MOLA) elevation data to provide a digital representation of Martian terrain.

2. How Does It Work?

The application processes MOLA MEGDR elevation data using Python, NumPy, and PDS4 Tools. It extracts elevation information and generates terrain visualizations, slope maps, and hazard maps.

Users can explore the Martian surface through interactive 2D maps and 3D terrain visualizations created using Plotly. The system also includes an A* pathfinding algorithm that identifies potential routes between selected starting and destination locations.

The route planner considers terrain-related factors such as elevation, slope, and hazard costs to identify comparatively suitable paths. It also provides route metrics and supports exporting route information in CSV and GeoJSON formats.

3. Key Features

  • Interactive Mars surface exploration.
  • Elevation and terrain visualization using NASA MOLA data.
  • Slope analysis and terrain hazard mapping.
  • Interactive 3D terrain visualization.
  • A* based terrain-aware route planning.
  • Selection of starting and destination locations.
  • Route metrics and CSV/GeoJSON export.
  • EVA-related estimates and checks to support exploration planning.

4. Technology Stack

The project uses Python and Streamlit for the web application, NumPy and PDS4 Tools for elevation data processing, Plotly for interactive visualization, and SciPy and Pillow for supporting data processing and image operations. The A* algorithm is used for route planning.

5. Benefits and Expected Impact

MARS EXPLORER provides an accessible way to understand Martian surface conditions and explore potential travel routes. Terrain-aware route planning can help identify comparatively less challenging paths and support preliminary exploration planning.

The platform demonstrates how planetary datasets, geospatial processing, and pathfinding algorithms can be combined to assist future astronaut mobility and mission planning.

6. Future Scope

Future improvements could include integrating additional high-resolution Mars imagery, geological information, thermal datasets, updated environmental observations, and more advanced terrain-risk models to make exploration planning more comprehensive.
